topic: Dissertation Literature Review: The Synthesis Matrix

copy.instagram:
Staring at a pile of 40 papers and feeling like your lit review is just a glorified book report? We’ve all been there—the 3 AM panic is real.

Most students fall into the 'Author-by-Author' trap, summarizing one paper after another. That’s a one-way ticket to a 2:2. To hit a First, you need to pivot to a Synthesis Matrix.

Slide 1: Stop listing authors. Start mapping debates.
Slide 2: Use a matrix to group papers by theme, not by date.
Slide 3: Contrast methodologies. Did one study have a tiny sample size? Point it out.
Slide 4: Identify the gap. Where does the current research stop and your work begin?

Stop summarizing and start synthesizing. If you’re stuck staring at a blank page, check the link in our bio for a deep dive into the synthesis method. Save this for when you’re deep in the research trenches.

copy.facebook:
Are you currently drowning in journal articles for your dissertation? I’ve seen so many brilliant students lose marks because their literature review feels like a list of summaries rather than a cohesive argument. 

If you find yourself organizing your chapters by author or year, you’re likely stuck in a 2:2 trap. The secret to a First-Class mark is thematic synthesis. Instead of describing what others found, you need to weigh their methodologies against each other and identify the exact gap your research is filling.

Here’s how to switch gears:
• Group your literature by theoretical debates, not by publication date.
• Critically contrast the limitations of different sampling methods.
• Clearly position your own research as the 'missing piece' in the conversation.
